resources.string: Installs the pinned DisplayXR stack on this tablet and performs the post-install steps that an APK install does not do.
Also install DisplayXR Browser (large download, ~326 MB)
Allow this app to install apps
Retry — ask Android for the confirmation again
Android will not let this app install anything until you allow it to install unknown apps. Nothing can be pre-granted here — Android requires the owner of the device to turn it on by hand.
Grant “Display over other apps” to the runtime

This one cannot be granted by an installer: SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW is an app-op, never granted at install and dropped by any uninstall+reinstall. Without it, see-through apps render on a BLACK background while 3D and weaving keep working — so it reads as a content bug rather than a missing permission.
Granted. Nothing more to do here.
What this installer does NOT do

• Each package is confirmed by Android separately. One tap here is still N confirmations — only a device owner or a privileged system app can install silently, and this is neither.

• It does not install the vendor display services. Those come from the vendor’s own private repo and install only because they carry the OEM’s signing key; this installer cannot fetch them and does not pretend to.

• It cannot grant CAMERA to Gaussian Splat or Avatar. Accept the prompt on their first launch, otherwise they open on a consent dialog instead of content.

• After a reboot, UNLOCK the tablet before opening any app. Launching a demo at the lockscreen crashes Model Viewer and Gaussian Splat (displayxr-runtime#1358).

• If an app was installed from a build signed with a different key, Android refuses the upgrade. This installer reports that rather than wiping the app’s data behind your back; uninstall that one app and run again.

The runtime is launched once automatically right after it installs. That single launch is what registers its OpenXRRuntimeBroker ContentProvider — until it happens, Android\'s FLAG_STOPPED keeps the provider unresolvable and every OpenXR app dies at instance creation with XR_ERROR_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE. Nothing clears it at boot, and it is the most common virgin-install failure.
